subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — monthly tokens & peak TPS
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — monthly tokens & peak TPS

Hi Sam,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the demo and for walking us through Acme's search+answer flow. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a tailored hosted-API pricing estimate: 

1) Workload overview (from the call)
- Primary use: in-product search & answer for logged-in users (supporting suggestions, Q&A)
- Typical prompt size: ~150 tokens input + ~200 tokens output on average

2) Questions we need to finalize pricing (can you confirm below):
- Expected monthly token volume (approx): _______
- Peak TPS (requests per second) during busy periods: _______
- Budget range you have in mind for the hosted API (monthly): _______
- Target cost target $/1M tokens (if you have a number): _______

From our side, I attached a simple pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx) that shows how cost scales with token volumes and three profile options (standard, optimized batching, and dedicated-reserved). If you can fill the blanks above or reply with ballpark numbers, we’ll run a few cost scenarios and share an estimated monthly bill plus recommended optimizations (batching, prefix cache, quantized model variants) that keep latency within your SLO.

Next steps I propose:
- You reply with approximate monthly tokens & peak TPS by EOD Tuesday.
- We produce a 1-page pricing estimate + ops notes (Ben will include notes on latency/peak handling).
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up to review (Ben available Wed/Thu).

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.example.com
(415) 555-0189

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmeanalytics.com>

Cc: Jane Park <jane.park@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — monthly tokens & peak TPS

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap and the worksheet — helpful. Answers below (these are estimates while we validate with engineering):

- Expected monthly token volume: ~120,000,000 tokens (120M) — this is based on 40k DAUs, ~75 tokens per session average.
- Peak TPS: ~25 TPS (we saw spikes up to ~30 TPS during end-of-month reporting, but typical peak is 20–25).
- Budget range: targeting $4,000–$6,000 / month for hosted inference initially.
- Target $/1M tokens: ideally <$35 per 1M tokens, but we can be flexible if latency/availability justifies a premium.

A couple of clarifying items: what latency SLO should we expect for the standard hosted option at our estimated peak TPS? Also, can you show a simple monthly cost breakdown at 120M tokens for both standard and optimized-batching profiles?

Happy to hop on a follow-up — Wed or Thu afternoon works.

Cheers,
Sam Lee
Head of Product | Acme Analytics
sam.lee@acmeanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — monthly tokens & peak TPS

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick numbers, that's perfect.

I pulled together two scenario estimates and added Ben's ops notes on latency and peak handling:

1) Standard hosted profile (no special batching) — estimate at 120M tokens:
- Estimated cost: ~$4,800 / month (rough)
- Expected median latency: ~220–300ms for generation at ~200-token outputs; 95th percentile can be higher during spikes.

2) Optimized batching + prefix caching profile — estimate at 120M tokens:
- Estimated cost: ~$3,600 / month (rough)
- Expected median latency: ~250–320ms (slightly higher median for batching but much better cost efficiency); 95th percentile improved with autoscale and cache warming.

Notes from Ben (ops):
- With a peak TPS of ~25, hosted autoscaling handles burst capacity; recommend enabling prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (saves ~20–30% tokens).
- If you need consistent sub-200ms P95, we should discuss a dedicated-reserved option (adds cost but reduces variability).

Next steps:
- I'll send a short PDF with the two line-item estimates and the recommended config.
- Ben to join follow-up to go over latency/scale tradeoffs — Wed 3pm PT works for us, does that fit your calendar?

If Wed 3pm doesn't work, propose Thu 2pm.

Thanks — will follow up with the PDF and a calendar invite once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.example.com
(415) 555-0189
